subject: Performance SLO & VPC Qualification \t6 network/latency questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC Qualification — next steps and checklist

Hi Samir — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we can validate performance for a Private/VPC deployment:

Summary of SLOs you called out:
- P95 inference latency target: <= 150 ms (token-level streaming expected)
- Sustained throughput: ~400 requests/sec (avg payloads ~250 tokens)
- Concurrency: ~80 concurrent live sessions (burst to 120)
- Streaming: yes — token-by-token streaming required for chat UX (we support HTTP/2 server-sent events or gRPC streaming)

Network & infra items we need to qualify for Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment:
- Network path: will you use VPC Peering, Transit Gateway peering, Direct Connect, or site-to-site VPN?
- Egress & bandwidth: confirm anticipated egress to Redwood hosts (estimate 1 Gbps baseline for your peak traffic)
- NAT / Load balancer: are outbound connections NATed via a single Elastic IP / NAT Gateway? Any SNAT limits?
- Internal latency budget: you mentioned <30 ms between application tier and model endpoint — please confirm 95/99 targets if available.
- Firewall / ports: TCP ports 443 (TLS) required outbound; any deep-packet inspection or proxy that might terminate TLS?
- Packet loss / jitter tolerance: please share SLOs for packet loss (e.g., <0.1%) and jitter if known.

Attachments: I attached a short Redwood network & SLO checklist (redwood_slo_network_checklist.pdf) and our suggested tests (ping, traceroute, iperf, HTTP/2 streaming checks).

Next steps:
1) Can you share a point of contact in Networking (email) so we can schedule a brief 30-min technical alignment?
2) Please confirm which private connectivity option you prefer (VPC Peering, Direct Connect, or VPN).
3) If possible, share a simple VPC diagram (subnets/NAT/egress) and any egress throughput limits.

If it helps, we can do an initial connectivity test (traceroute/iperf) from our test agents once we have a contact and an agreed window.

Thanks — I’ll loop Jonas in on the technical thread.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
https://redwood.example/docs/slo-checklist

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Networking <netops@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:20:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC Qualification — next steps and checklist

Thanks Marissa — quick answers from our side and attaching a basic VPC diagram. See inline:

- Connectivity: We prefer Direct Connect to avoid public egress where possible; VPC Peering is also an option between our prod VPC and your hosted VPC if needed.
- Region: Primary workloads in us-west-2 (Oregon).
- Egress/Bandwidth: We can provision ~1 Gbps initially; we have headroom to scale to 2.5 Gbps if needed but would require ticketing lead time.
- NAT/Proxies: Outbound is currently through a pair of NAT gateways; no explicit SNAT limits but we do have connection tracking limits on the NAT instances we can raise with NetOps.
- Internal latency: App tier to model endpoint target is p95 <= 30 ms; p99 we aim for <= 60 ms.
- Packet loss: typically <0.05% within our AZ; cross-AZ varies and we can provide measurements.
- TLS termination: We do not terminate TLS in our egress — traffic goes through standard NAT. If we engage Direct Connect, we can keep traffic entirely private.

Point of contact for NetOps: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@acme.com> (cc'd on the attachment I sent). She can take the technical scheduling.

I attached our VPC diagram (acme_vpc_diagram.pdf). Happy to schedule the technical sync — afternoons PST work best for our network team.

- Samir
Principal Product Manager, Acme Retail
samir.patel@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC Qualification — next steps and checklist

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks for the quick follow-up and for sharing the diagram. That all sounds workable. A few follow-ups and proposed times for a technical sync:

Items from our side:
- Streaming protocol: Redwood Private supports HTTP/2 (SSE) and gRPC streaming. For token-level streaming we recommend HTTP/2 SSE in environments that have proxies/legacy infrastructure; gRPC works well over Direct Connect. Please let us know if you have a preference.
- Tests we will run with your NetOps during the window: TCP traceroute, 100MB iperf3 test to measure throughput, and a synthetic HTTP/2 streaming session to measure token latency under load.
- Firewall checks: confirm outbound 443 allowed to our egress IPs (we'll provide a short-lived allowlist if you want to restrict).
- Sizing guidance: to meet p95<=150ms and 400 RPS sustained, our initial Dedicated footprint recommendation is 4x A40-sized GPU nodes behind the load balancer with prefix caching enabled. We’ll finalize sizing after initial traffic profiles and tests.

Proposed technical sync windows (PST):
- Fri 13 Nov, 3:00–3:30pm PST
- Mon 16 Nov, 9:00–9:30am PST
- Mon 16 Nov, 1:30–2:00pm PST

Can you confirm which works for Priya / NetOps? Once confirmed we’ll share a dial-in and a test plan doc.

Thanks — Jonas will join as our infrastructure lead for the call.

Best,
Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC Qualification — next steps and checklist

Thanks all — I can make the Fri 3pm PST slot. I’ll prepare the test endpoints and a list of our egress IPs for a short-lived allowlist. A couple of notes from infra:
- We recommend using Direct Connect if Acme can provision it — it reduces jitter and avoids NAT connection tracking limits.
- For streaming resiliency we support automatic reconnect + resume for in-flight tokens; if the network path has jitter >20ms we’ll add a small client-side rebuffering allowance.
- I’ll also surface a short internal checklist for Priya on expected firewall rules and MTU considerations for Direct Connect.

Looking forward to the call — see you Fri.

4A9 Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
